publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: The paper is based on the results of a wide-ranging literature search and the experience the authors have gained in passive intermodulation products (PIMP) measurements over the last two years. The purpose is to give an overview of recent research relative to the investigation of PIMP in antenna systems. It describes briefly the types of passive non-linearities, mechanisms responsible for the generation of PIMP, guidelines for minimising PIMP generation, techniques for locating passive non-linearities, analysis of higher order PIMP and the study of various types of components, including feeders, reflectors, feeds, multicouplers and duplexers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The suppression of intermodulation product generation in materials and structures used in radio communications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: Describes a research programme aimed at providing a practical engineering solution to suppressing structural intermodulation interferences. The results are useful not just to mobile radio communication services, but to satellite communication or any radio installation where intermodulation effects are prevalent due to a multiplicity of systems. A brief survey was done on the mechanism of structural intermodulation. A more probable mechanism based on metal-semiconductor rectifying effect is suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Passive intermodulation products in antennas-an overview
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: Provides an insight into techniques currently used to produce microwave reflector antennas with very low passive intermodulation products (PIMP) production. Although the principles expounded are generally accepted, the author concentrates on antennas for satellite ground station application. To give a perspective, modern microwave antennas are in some applications required to give a performance of around 120 to 150 dB down on carriers with powers ranging from a few hundred watts to several kilowatts per channel. For the tightest specifications, even small contributions to PIMP must be considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The control of passive intermodulation products in spacecraft antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: Considers those aspects of design which affect passive intermodulation products (PIMP) control. The feed and reflector design aspects concentrate on antennas having combined transmit/receive feed chains whose operation is particularly sensitive to PIMP generation. Suitable reflector construction techniques are also considered in order to achieve acceptable PIMP performance at antenna subsystem level. System integration considerations include the thermal control of the high power feed chain and its dissipative components (diplexer) as well as the positioning of thermal blankets for controlling temperature of the antenna subsystem in the space environment. Measured test results at L- and Ku-band are included with PIMP orders ranging from 9th to 21st at L-band and 21st to 27th at Ku band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of the intermodulation product performance of reflector antennas and related structures by microwave imaging
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: Reports upon further developments that have been made in the adaptation of the microwave imaging technique to locate sources of intermodulation produce (IMP) generation upon microwave reflectors and related structures. The objective of this research work is two fold. Firstly it is hoped to provide a new means of evaluating the IMP performance of reflector antennas and, by locating the sources of IMP present, to show how it might be possible to improve the IMP performance by reducing or eliminating these sources. Secondly, it is hoped that by using the imaging process it may be possible to study to the causes and effects of IMP generation upon reflectors and similar such structures. For conventional microwave imaging and antenna metrology, the target under investigation is illuminated at a single frequency and acts as a passive scatterer to this illumination. In the present case however, the object is illuminated by high power source feeds at least two different frequencies, inducing an active response in the form of IMP generation. All measurements and data evaluation are then performed at the frequency of the chosen IMP signal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the IMP signal phase relationship to reflector antennas and feeds
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: Previous published results on the origin of intermodulation products (IMP) have concentrated on measurement of the scalar amplitude of the IMP signals relative to the applied signal levels. When making complex amplitude and phase measurements of IMP signals it can be shown that the phase of the IMP signal generated at any point contact or junction can be predicted relative to the phase of the exciting source signals irrespective of the nonlinear characteristic, applied signal levels or the subsequent IMP amplitude. Work carried out by the authors into the microwave imaging of IMP sources on reflector antennas is believed to include the first published experimental results of measurements of both the amplitude and phase of IMP signals at microwave frequencies. The paper reports upon further investigations involving measurements of IMP signal phase and suggests how knowledge and application of the phase relationship could be an aid to predicting and evaluating the IMP field radiated by a reflector that is generating IMP upon its surface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and improvement of PIMP measurement facilities and the measurement of PIMP in antenna structures
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: The paper is based on the authors' experience of developing passive intermodulation products (PIMP) measurement systems for testing materials and structural components. Its purpose is to discuss some design considerations in developing such facilities and the various ways of improving the system performance. The topics discussed are summarised as follows: current PIMP measurement techniques; power combining and sampling devices; the design of test chambers and their performance; the criteria for selecting linear dummy load and some test results; some suggestions for improving the laboratory PIMP measurement system; and the measurement of PIMPs generated in an aluminium antenna structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Test set for the measurement of IMDS at 900 MHz
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Passive Intermodulation Products in Antennas and Related Structures
abstract: The rapid growth in the number of subscribers and the highly time variable patterns of use in cellular mobile radio systems are creating severe channel congestion on radio cell-sites in urban areas. It is for this reason that a further increase in the number of co-sited base stations per cell is contemplated, which may lead in turn to excessive generation of unwanted intermodulation products (IMDs). These could become one of the major obstacles for an improved utilization of the limited available RF spectrum. An experimental test bench for the measurement of IMD products, generated by various components of a base station multicoupler system at 900 MHz is described. It is anticipated that such a set-up needs to provide for the measurement of IMD levels as low as -100 dBc for various frequency spacings, between co-sited transmitters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
